title: Manchester United lock in Bruno Fernandes until 2028, but the results still bite
body:
Manchester United have triggered a one-year extension on captain Bruno Fernandes' deal, which now runs until 2028 [S1]. Sky Sports ran the same story and described it as the club activating its 12-month option to extend the skipper's contract [S2]. Before anyone starts planning a parade, remember that a clause being used is paperwork, not a plot twist.

The extension is sensible housekeeping, and the captain's future is now written down. But a contract clause is a box ticked, not a trophy won, and the side still have to turn that security into results on the pitch.

The results tell the less comfortable story. Across their last five league matches they have won none, drawn two and lost three, collecting 2 points [ST1]. They have scored 5 and conceded 14, with the run reading DLLDL [ST1]. Those figures point to a leaky back line rather than a side short of a signature, and no transfer headline changes that.

Talk is cheap until the paperwork is signed, so treat every rumour with care, especially the ones dressed up as certainties.

The Touchline Take: judge the business when the window shuts, not before.
